paper.title_en: Generation of UL-Axions by a Kerr Black Hole. Part III: The fate of its Axion Wind
paper.abstract_en: In two previous articles, we have explained how super-massive Kerr Black Holes in the nucleus of an active galaxy or quasar can generate a large amount of axion particles in their magnetosphere. In that third part, we explore the possibility of observable dynamics resulting from some interaction of an axion wind with the baryonic matter and the axionic Dark Matter in the surroundings of the closest AGNs. The axions that we have considered are the same as those Ultra Light Axions favored in cosmology as the main content of Dark Matter and which form Bose-Einstein Condensates, supporting a gigantic Schrödinger wave. In the paper we investigate what can be the nature of the interaction of the axion wind with the plasma and the hydrogen gas in the host galaxy and its halo. Despite the intriguing nature of a possible interaction, we show that only a kind of gravitational Tcherenkov-Vavilov effect can be efficiently operating with acoustic waves through a streaming instability. The instability is fast enough to operate efficiently in the central region of the host galaxy up to parsec scales and makes Lyman-alpha diagnostics of the acoustic waves of hydrogen gas and plasma possible, as well as the detection its hyperfine emission at 21 cm. However it turns out that scattering of the axion wind is very long and thus these winds could travel over very large distances and cross other galaxies. And then the wind travels without significant loss along its halo and even beyond up to quantum thermalization, which makes possible direct detection of these axions by conversion into gamma-rays on Earth, opening a possible axion astronomy in the local Universe. The parameters of Messier 87 indicate that it is a good candidate for developing these investigations both through the conversion of axions into gamma-rays and Lyman alpha diagnosis in the bulge.
